report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Implement claim parsing and judging of findings against repository symbol definitions.

symbols.name: claim_text
symbols.note: Strips a severity-prefixed location column from a finding's raw text.

symbols.name: candidate_names
symbols.note: Extracts candidate symbol names from text using a regex.

symbols.name: judge
symbols.note: Classifies a finding as false, false-elsewhere, scoped, or undecided.

claims.text: The assertion, with any ``<where> | <severity> | ...`` prefix stripped.
claims.why: The function splits on '|' and, when parts[1] is a severity, returns parts[2], which is the text after the first two pipe-separated fields, thus stripping the prefix.

claims.text: MEASURED: without this split, ``_resolve_store | medium | Mentions refusing paths under memory/ but code is truncated; the check may be missing`` was scored provably false because ``_resolve_store`` is defined -- but the finding never claimed otherwise. It is about a check INSIDE that function. Reading the location column as the subject manufactures a lie out of an honest observation.
claims.why: The example shows that without stripping, the location column '_resolve_store' would be treated as the subject; the code's split strips it, preserving the actual assertion about a check inside the function.

claims.text: Decide whether one finding is provably wrong about the repository.
claims.why: The function implements a decision procedure returning a verdict tuple based on whether the named symbol is defined in the module, elsewhere, or scoped.

claims.text: ``false`` the named symbol is defined in the module it is claimed absent from
claims.why: The code checks if any candidate name is in the module's defined set (and not borrowed), returning 'false' with the names.

claims.text: ``false-elsewhere`` it exists, in another module -- wrong about WHERE, which is a different error needing a different repair
claims.why: The code checks if any candidate name is defined in any module's defined set, returning 'false-elsewhere' with those names.

claims.text: ``scoped`` the claim limits itself to the window its reader saw, so it asserts nothing about the program
claims.why: The code checks _SELF_SCOPED regex on the text and returns 'scoped' if matched.
The function returns 'undecided' in several branches: when not an existence claim, when module not in index, when named symbol is imported, or when no symbol resolves.

claims.text: It can prove a finding false. It can never prove one true.
claims.why: The function only returns 'false' or 'false-elsewhere' as negative verdicts; it never returns a positive 'true' verdict, only 'undecided' or 'scoped'.

claims.text: The named symbol is defined in the module it is claimed absent from
claims.why: The code returns 'false' when hits are found, i.e., names in the module's defined set.

claims.text: It exists, in another module -- wrong about WHERE
claims.why: The code returns 'false-elsewhere' when names exist in any module's defined set.

claims.text: The claim limits itself to the window its reader saw
This cannot tell. Not a pass.
claims.why: All undecided returns are present and do not indicate a pass.

claims.text: claims absence, but <names> is defined in <module>
claims.why: The message is constructed with the hits list and module name.

claims.text: claims absence, but <names> exists elsewhere in the repository
claims.why: The message is constructed with the everywhere names.

observations.what: The _ABSENCE and _SELF_SCOPED regexes are not defined in this chunk; they are referenced but not shown.
The _NAME regex is not defined in this chunk; it is used in candidate_names.
_SEVERITIES is not defined in this chunk; it is used in claim_text.
The function candidate_names returns a set of names but does not validate against any known symbol list; it is purely regex-based.

The judge function checks 'borrowed' to avoid false positives when a name is imported, but the logic only returns 'undecided' if the name is borrowed; if a name is both defined and borrowed, it is treated as defined (since hits excludes borrowed).
The judge function does not handle the case where a name appears in both defined and borrowed sets for the module; it will treat it as defined only if it is in defined and not in borrowed.

The 'false-elsewhere' check uses 'any(n in s for s in defined.values())' which may include the current module's defined set; if a name is defined in the current module but not in the 'here' set due to borrowing, it could be misclassified.
The function claim_text returns the raw text if the prefix is not a recognized severity, which might leave a location column in the text, potentially causing false positives in judge.
